findings: The topic runs from printed page 54 to 75; the lesson keeps all thirteen numbered organelle sections in the textbook's order.
The textbook's sentence that the nucleus 'synthesises ribosomes' via nucleoli is kept as printed; the ribosome section explains that nucleoli make the subunits.
Lysosomes are said to be discovered in the 'mid-18th century' by de Duve, who worked in the twentieth century; the lesson omits the century and records the printed error here.
Fibres of the cytoskeleton: the textbook gives no dimensions; the figure's approximate widths (7, 25 and 10 nm) are standard values added for scale and marked 'about'.
